why:
phase-467 — the process-wide default threshold, reachable from C. The byte itself lives in `nros_log` (RFC-0019: the Rust API is the implementation, C delegates); this is a pointer-free forwarder onto `nros_log::Logger::set_default_level` / `::default_level`.

EXTENSION, and the reason is the recorded surface rather than upstream's design: rcl's counterpart is `rcutils_logging_set_default_logger_level` / `..._get_default_logger_level`, which the recorded rclc surface does not carry, so there is no upstream row to correlate against — the same reason `c:logger_set_level` and `c:logger_get_level` are extensions. The SHAPE is rcutils's, including the one inversion: `UNSET` on the DEFAULT restores `INFO` (`RCUTILS_DEFAULT_LOGGER_DEFAULT_LEVEL`) rather than taking a level away, because the default has nothing to inherit from.

It exists because `RCLC_LOG_SEVERITY_UNSET` became INHERIT in phase-467 (row `c:log_severity_t`), and an inheritance whose target no C image can move is a capability stated in a header and reachable from one language. `rclc_logger_set_level(rclc_log_default_logger(), ..)` is NOT this: that moves the threshold of the one logger NAMED "nros".
